definitions.explanation: Describes the natural process of a memory becoming less clear or vivid over time. Used for personal memories, collective memory, and historical awareness.

examples.japanese: {記憶|きおく}が{薄|うす}れてきた。
examples.english: My memory has started to fade.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}が{経|た}つにつれて{記憶|きおく}が{薄|うす}れていく。
examples.english: As time passes, memories fade away.

examples.japanese: {震災|しんさい}の{記憶|きおく}が{薄|うす}れないように、{毎年|まいとし}{追悼|ついとう}{式|しき}が{行|おこな}われている。
examples.english: A memorial ceremony is held every year so that the memory of the earthquake disaster does not fade.

notes:
Composed of {記憶|きおく} (memory) + が (subject marker) + {薄|うす}れる (to thin, to fade). The verb {薄|うす}れる conveys the image of something becoming thinner or lighter, like color fading. It captures the gradual, natural loss of clarity in memories.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {記憶|きおく}が{薄|うす}れていく: memory gradually fades
- {記憶|きおく}が{薄|うす}れないうちに: while the memory is still fresh
- {記憶|きおく}が{薄|うす}れないように: so that the memory doesn't fade

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {記憶|きおく}が{消|き}える: memory disappears — stronger than fading; suggests complete loss
- {忘|わす}れる: to forget — the active verb for forgetting; {薄|うす}れる emphasizes the gradual process rather than the result
- {記憶|きおく}が{曖昧|あいまい}になる: memory becomes vague — focuses on loss of precision rather than intensity
